seo.title: Enterprise Agentic Engineering with VSA | SSW Training
seo.description: Build reliable agentic features with Vertical Slice Architecture. A hands-on SSW course mentored by Daniel Mackay and Gordon Beeming.

blocks.heading: Enterprise Agentic Engineering **with VSA**
blocks.description: Start with a slice. Build an agent you can trust. Daniel Mackay and Gordon Beeming kick off with Vertical Slice Architecture, then guide developers through the engineering decisions that make agentic features easier to build, test and operate.

image.altText: Illustration of Daniel Mackay and Gordon Beeming discussing software architecture at a desk

blocks.heading: Agent demos are easy. Reliable features take engineering.
blocks.subtitle: Agentic systems cross model calls, tools, data and user workflows. A clear feature boundary makes change easier to reason about and results easier to check.

cards.title: Make change easier to reason about
cards.description: Keep the request, orchestration, dependencies and tests close to the feature they serve.

cards.title: Design for uncertain behaviour
cards.description: Define what the agent may do, when a human needs to step in, and how to check the result.

cards.title: Prepare for real use
cards.description: Work through permissions, traceability, failure handling and release decisions.

blocks.heading: Begin with **Vertical Slice Architecture**
blocks.subtitle: Dan and Gordon start with one user action and trace it through a self-contained feature slice. This gives the rest of the course a shared structure for building agentic behaviour. Each slice keeps its request, handler, local dependencies and tests together.

cards.title: One capability
cards.description: Organise code around a business action.

cards.title: One clear path
cards.description: Follow the request through to the result.

cards.title: Local dependencies
cards.description: Keep tool and data access close to the slice.

cards.title: Focused tests
cards.description: Check behaviour alongside the code that delivers it.

blocks.heading: From first slice to **production thinking**
blocks.description: Follow one feature from its first architecture decision through agentic behaviour, evaluation and release.

items.heading: 01 · Kick off with VSA
items.description: Turn a business action into a self-contained feature. Identify its request, handler, local dependencies and tests. Use the slice to make ownership and change impact visible.

items.heading: 02 · Add agentic behaviour
items.description: Define the agent’s goal, allowed tools, inputs and output contract. Decide what remains deterministic and what can be delegated to a model.

items.heading: 03 · Build reliable tool use
items.description: Connect the agent to a narrow capability. Cover permissions, validation, idempotency and useful failure paths before adding more tools.

items.heading: 04 · Evaluate and observe
items.description: Create representative scenarios, inspect traces and test outcomes. Review cost, latency and quality together.

items.heading: 05 · Ship an enterprise slice
items.description: Walk through release, monitoring, human review and rollback choices. Leave with a repeatable checklist for the next agentic feature.

blocks.heading: Designed for teams **building real software**
blocks.subtitle: Practical architecture and implementation decisions, taught through one evolving feature.

cards.title: Audience
cards.description: Experienced developers, architects and technical leads

cards.title: Learning style
cards.description: Mentor-led discussion, code exercises and review

cards.title: Takeaway
cards.description: A repeatable approach to building and reviewing agentic features

blocks.heading: Dan & Gordon
blocks.subtitle:
Dan brings more than 20 years of software experience and deep .NET expertise. He helps teams turn architecture principles into maintainable code and starts this course with a practical VSA exercise.

Gordon helps teams adopt DevOps practices and improve the way they build and release software. He joins Dan to turn the initial slice into an agentic feature and examine how the design holds up in an enterprise setting.

faqs.question: Who is this for?
faqs.answer: Developers, software architects and technical leads who already build production applications and want a practical approach to agentic features.

faqs.question: Do participants need VSA experience?
faqs.answer: No prior VSA experience is needed. Dan and Gordon start with the core principles and a worked feature slice.

faqs.question: Which agent framework will be used?
faqs.answer: The exercises focus on architecture and engineering decisions that apply across agent frameworks.

faqs.question: What will I take away?
faqs.answer: A worked feature slice and a practical checklist for designing, evaluating and operating agentic features.
